ownerDecisions.source: owner (Q-I5-4) and lane monitor (owner-delegated Q-I5-1..3), relayed by the lane monitor
ownerDecisions.decision: I05 v4 decisions, 2026-10-16. Owner: Q-I5-4 = (a). The BIND's (pid, starttime) must be a member; other members don't refuse. Monitor (owner-delegated): Q-I5-1 = (a): a fresh read at every BIND_EXECUTION. Q-I5-2 = (a): every observation failure refuses with the existing WORKER_NOT_OBSERVED, non-fatal and retryable, journaled locally, with no wire change. Q-I5-3 = (a): pidfd-confirmed: cgroup.procs → pidfd_open → stat starttime and cgroup check → pidfd still not exited. Defaults B1, B4 and B6 hold as you stated. So I05 v4 is a model, vectors and README successor; the v3 frame schema bytes and its supplement stay byte-identical.

ownerDecisions.source: lane monitor (decision text and published pointers)
ownerDecisions.decision: Nothing in R10 fixes B1-B6. The merged R10 gate (HE-003D) keeps observedWorkers as a signed configuration list that must be EMPTY, and it refuses a non-empty list (owner Q-HE3D-2 (a): BIND fails closed until the I05 successor). That rule is removed by the R10 packet that adopts your I05 v4. So I05 v4 DEFINES B1-B6, and R10 follows it. Binding constraints from published contracts: 1. Seccomp allowlists v4 (main), EFFECT_GATE: only syscalls on that allowlist are usable. 2. Owner Q-HE2S-G (b): the gate opens files only via openat on dir fds (no std::fs opens). 3. Matrix v5 (main): only the probe-worker leaf READ, search on its two parents, and procAccess to planeon_worker_t; the worker is other-uid, so only cgroup.procs, stat and status are reachable. 4. HS43 precedent (owner Q-HS43-1 (a)): the identity is pid plus the start time from /proc/<pid>/stat, race-free where possible (pidfd); a pidfd for another process needs pidfd_open.

ownerDecisions.decision:
241: both readings are correct, so record them as the monitor's confirmations.

(ii) The cgroup check as a second cgroup.procs read with the pidfd held is what I meant. It's within C3 and the leaf-only grant, and it's race-free.

carriedFindings.IR5-1: carried (NOTE): IR4-1 is answered both ways: two workers per answer, and README:304-306 now says what is pinned. One partial reordering is still unpinned, and the README discloses it: an early liveness check, run before the v3 checks, that refuses a PID with no process at all. Neither OUTSIDER (5100, alive) nor WRONG_START (alive leaf member) has a gone PID. The vectors catch this check only through the local log's step label at O05, and not at all if the check logs as step 1. The wire answer then changes from a permanent v3 refusal to a retryable WORKER_NOT_OBSERVED, which is IR2-1's symptom. A plausible R10 shape for this is 'pidfd_open first to pin the process'. R10 owns the log format, so R10 may not replay the log labels.
